messages:
raj: CI alert — infra repo apply is stuck on the GHA job `helm-sync`. It times out after 15m and blocks the terraform apply queue. Happened 3x in the last hour.

raj: Logs show `Error: context deadline exceeded` and then the job never creates new pods. Not sure if it's a GHA concurrency/caching issue or cluster capacity.

olivia: can you paste the helm-sync step log and the GH action run id?

raj: run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/runs/74231234 (internal)
raj: helm-sync snippet:
```
2026-02-26T14:12:03Z Starting helm sync for release gpu-pool
2026-02-26T14:12:10Z Waiting for resources: daemonset/gpu-driver, deployment/gpu-allocator
2026-02-26T14:27:10Z error: context deadline exceeded
2026-02-26T14:27:10Z helm sync failed, will retry later
```

maria: hmm we also saw cache restore warnings earlier in the run? Could be GHA cache causing step replay oddities. Any `restore-cache` step errors?

raj: yeah `actions/cache@v3` logged: `Cache restore hit but failed integrity check, skipping`. Then `helm-sync` started, eventual timeout.

zane: two things to check: 1) Are GPU nodepools autoscaling/preempting? 2) Are helm hooks creating Jobs that wait for PVCs and block? We had a similar case where `helm upgrade --wait` hung because new pods were `0/1 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu`.

raj: I ran `kubectl get pods -n infra -o wide` and saw pods pending:
```
NAME                          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
gpu-allocator-5d6f8b7d9-abc   0/1     Pending   0          10m   <none>
```
kubectl describe pod shows:
```
Events:
  2m    Warning   FailedScheduling  pod/gpu-allocator-5d6f8b7d9-abc  0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

olivia: that points to capacity. Did autoscaler log any scale-ups?

sre-bot: {incident} us-west-2 GPU nodepool experiencing intermittent maintenance — 2/5 nodes drained (ETA 45m). Affected deployments may see Insufficient resource errors.

maria: if nodes are draining, helm `--wait` will block until pods are scheduled — that fits. But why does the workflow not fail fast? We have 15m timeout but the job retried and ended up blocking apply. We should avoid long blocking steps in the apply pipeline.

raj: suggestion: add a pre-check step `kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu}'` and fail early if capacity < threshold. Also optionally set `helm upgrade --timeout 5m` during CI.

zane: also bump GHA concurrency control to prevent parallel applies targeting same cluster: current `concurrency: infra-apply-${{ github.ref }}` collides when multiple branches run. Maybe use `concurrency: infra-apply-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.sha }}`? or lock via `gh actions lock`?

maria: we had cache key collisions — trying to reuse action caches across different runner sizes can cause integrity skips. For now, workaround: in infra workflows set `restore-keys` narrower and add `if: success() || failure()` cleanup step.

olivia: action items: 1) raj — open a runbook PR that adds pre-check capacity and reduces helm timeout to 5m for CI. 2) zane — propose concurrency/lock change in workflows. 3) eng-infra ops — monitor us-west-2 nodepool and notify when maintenance completes.

raj: creating PR now with the helm timeout and pre-check, will include `kubectl get cs` check and an explicit guard: `if [ "$GPU_AVAILABLE" -lt 2 ]; then exit 1; fi` so CI fails fast.

ci-bot: Re-run suggestion: `gh run rerun 74231234 --job helm-sync` (admins only) — consider manual retry after nodepool stable.

zane: also optional: switch helm-sync step to do `helm diff` first and skip upgrade when only irrelevant chart metadata changed. Saves churn.

maria: sounds good. Raj please tag me on the PR, will review fast.

raj: will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
